description: Resolve an error issue, as in Sentry: the game's owner has fixed it or accepts it (a GPU driver's error on test phones, one the newest build fixed). The Errors page hides it, glitchless_get_error lists it apart, and glitchless_triage, the overview and the weekly summary leave it out. It comes back by itself if players hit it again in a version later than the newest players had hit it in (any_version: in any version, the old builds included), first in the list and new to the new_error alert. Store test phones (Google Play runs each upload on its own before release), bots, testers and dev builds don't bring it back unless all_sessions is true. fingerprint is the issue's from glitchless_get_error or glitchless_triage (error-<fingerprint>), or the start of one. Resolving one again (one that came back) starts over from now. clear: true unresolves it. Without fingerprint, lists the game's resolved errors. Only the person's say-so resolves an error: ask before resolving one. Needs an Owner's or Admin's key, as alert settings do.

all_sessions.description: Come back when any session fires it (store test phones, bots, testers, dev builds), not only a player's

any_version.description: Come back if it fires again in any version, not only a later one

fingerprint.description: The issue's fingerprint, e.g. "9803ec1a", or the start of one

game.description: The game, by name or id, when signed in to a workspace (glitchless_list_games lists them); later calls keep it. With a key for one game (gl_sk_…), a call that names another game is refused: sign in to the workspace to reach every game.

note.description: Why, in a few words (200 characters at most), e.g. "Google Play's test phones on SwiftShader"

name: glitchless_resolve_error
title: Resolve error
